Estimate Resistance Profiles From a Fitted Joint Bernoulli Model

Source: R/profile_estimate.R
profile_estimate.Rd

Produces per-event joint-profile estimates under one of three EXPLICITLY DIFFERENT estimands – estimand has no default, by design:

Usage

profile_estimate(
  fit_result,
  design,
  Y,
  ids,
  estimand,
  n_draws = 500L,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  seed = 123L
)

Arguments

fit_result

List from profile_fit_joint_bernoulli (reads $fit), or a raw cmdstanr CmdStanMCMC.

design

List from profile_build_design (reads $stan_data and $design$states).

Y, ids

The SAME Y matrix and ids data frame passed to profile_build_design.

estimand

Character, one of "unconditional", "observed_preserving_conditional", "missing_allocation". No default – the caller must choose.

n_draws

Integer. Posterior draws used (subsampled if the fit has more). Default 500L. Note: for "unconditional"/ "observed_preserving_conditional", the returned profile_probability_draws array is n_draws x nrow(Y) x 2^D – memory scales with all three, so reduce n_draws for a very large Y with a large panel.

ci_level

Numeric in (0, 1). Credible-interval level for profile_probability_lower/upper and class_probability_lower/upper. Default 0.95 (giving the [Q_.025, Q_.975] marginal CrI). Ignored for estimand = "missing_allocation" (its uncertainty is already the full set of discrete per-draw allocations, not a further interval). These are MARGINAL per-event/per-class/per-state CrIs, each computed by aggregating WITHIN a draw first (summing state probabilities into a class margin, say) and taking quantiles ACROSS draws second – never the reverse, and never a simultaneous region across multiple events/classes/states at once.

seed

Integer. Default 123L.

Value

A list with estimand (echoes the argument, for provenance) and state_labels (character vector, length 2^D, e.g. "RRSS"), plus:

"unconditional" / "observed_preserving_conditional"

profile_probability: matrix, events x 2^D states, the posterior-mean probability of each state per event; profile_probability_lower/profile_probability_upper: same shape, the ci_level marginal CrI per event x state; profile_probability_draws: the full n_draws x events x 2^D array; class_probability/ class_probability_lower/class_probability_upper: matrix, events x D classes – the per-class resistance margin (states summed WITHIN each draw, then meaned/quantiled across draws), with its own CrI, not derived by summing the per-state CrIs (that would NOT be a valid interval for the sum)); class_probability_draws: the full n_draws x events x D array behind class_probability (e.g. for feeding profile_check_sampler's derived_estimates MCSE check).

"missing_allocation"

allocated_state: integer matrix, n_draws x events, each entry a state index into state_labels.

Details

"unconditional"

The model's own implied profile distribution from an event's covariates alone, ignoring whatever was actually tested for that event. A population-level baseline, never a per-patient "best guess" when AST results exist for that patient.

"observed_preserving_conditional"

Never overwrites a tested cell: distributes probability mass only over the states compatible with the event's own observed R/S pattern (via profile_compatible_states) – exactly the same exact marginalization the Stan model's own likelihood already uses for untested classes, not an approximation. A fully-tested event collapses to 100 reduces exactly to the unconditional distribution (every state is "compatible" when nothing was tested). This is the estimand DALY-style burden calculations need: never claim to know more about a patient's resistance pattern than was actually measured.

"missing_allocation"

Like "observed_preserving_conditional", but instead of a continuous probability over compatible states, DRAWS one specific state per event per posterior draw from that same conditional distribution – carrying allocation uncertainty forward as a set of discrete posterior draws, for downstream calculations that need an actual profile assignment per patient (e.g. counting how many patients fall in profile RRRR) with Monte Carlo uncertainty across draws, rather than fractional probability mass.
